# Cedric Stanhope

## Overview

- **Age:** 19 years old (by volume 4)  <sub>[v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002), [v4 c3 P7](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0007)</sub>
- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c1 P49](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0049)</sub>
- **Origin:** United States (Boston)  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045)</sub>
- **Role:** Student and poet  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v4 c3 P33](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0033)</sub>

## Appearance

In his childhood, Cedric had a tiny, exquisite face with delicate features, dark blue eyes, and chestnut curls. As he grew into manhood, he reached a height of six feet and replaced his curls with short-cut brown hair. He closely resembles his father in countenance and eye color.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c19 P26](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0026), [v2 c23 P27](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0027), [v2 c27 P24](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0024), [v3 c40 P2](../source/v03-c40.md#nw-v03-c40-p0002), [v4 c3 P30](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0030)_

## Personality

Cedric possesses a grave, meditative, and thoughtful nature paired with an imaginative mind that envisions fairy tales, rock people, and poetic ideas. He is polite, gentle, and well-behaved, though he exhibits strong manliness, dignity, and a firm sense of patriotism and fairness. Deeply affectionate toward his family and kindred spirits, he forms enduring bonds of friendship and retains his warm, imaginative spirit as he matures.

_Sources: [v2 c5 P8](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0008), [v2 c8 P52](../source/v02-c08.md#nw-v02-c08-p0052), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038), [v2 c15 P1](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0001), [v2 c15 P14](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0014), [v2 c19 P32](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0032), [v2 c19 P33](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0033), [v2 c27 P5](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0005), [v2 c27 P30](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0030), [v3 c23 P6](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0006), [v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032), [v4 c3 P33](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0033)_

## History

Cedric came from the United States to Brierley at age ten to reside with his grandmother, Mrs. Stanhope. Enrolling at Brierley school, he instantly formed a deep friendship with his teacher, Nell Harcourt, who appreciated his imaginative ideas and intellect. During his school years, he defended his American flag in a match with St. Clair Trask, protected younger boys, and courted his classmate Gracie Pullen. Nell introduced him to Miss Rosalind Penrose, with whom he shared imaginative 'dream-people' and formed a warm bond. When his father, Stephen Stanhope, arrived for a surprise visit, Cedric's letters helped facilitate Stephen's reunion and subsequent marriage to Miss Rosalind. Cedric celebrated their wedding by ringing a brass dinner bell that stirred the local echoes. Following the wedding, he moved to Boston with his father and stepmother, returning to Echo Cottage for summer vacations. As he matured into a tall young man of nineteen, he published poetry in magazines and prepared for two years of study abroad in Europe.

## Background by volume

- Born in the United States to Stephen Stanhope and his late mother  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c15 P2](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0002)</sub>
- Sent to Brierley to live with his paternal grandmother after his mother's death  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c11 P38](../source/v02-c11.md#nw-v02-c11-p0038)</sub>
- Raised under strict traditional moral and eating principles by his grandmother  <sub>[v2 c15 P12](../source/v02-c15.md#nw-v02-c15-p0012), [v2 c19 P10](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0010)</sub>

## Quotes

> I ask you to take these, teacher, which I discovered in the field belonging to Mr. Duckett, and I returned so I could offer them to you since I believed you were a lady who would appreciate them, and also because . . . teacher, I am fond of you.  <sub>[v2 c5 P21](../source/v02-c05.md#nw-v02-c05-p0021)</sub>

> I ask that you be seated here, teacher; while my spot will be down by your feet. Would you mind if I rest my head against your knee? Sitting together in this manner was the custom for my little mother and me. Oh, I feel this is truly wonderful.  <sub>[v2 c19 P26](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0026)</sub>

> Grandma permits me to drink a glass of milk and eat a piece of bread and butter prior to going to sleep; and when it is Sunday night she spreads jam on the bread. Therefore I am consistently pleased when Sunday night arrives . . . owing to several reasons.  <sub>[v2 c27 P30](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0030)</sub>

> Teacher, you will never age. You belong to those lucky human beings who discovered and imbibed the Fountain of Youth,—you alongside Mother Rosalind. Look at this! After you get married, calling you Mrs. Carrow is something I WILL NOT do. For me, your name will forever be 'Teacher’—the instructor who gave me the finest lessons I was ever taught.  <sub>[v4 c3 P32](../source/v04-c03.md#nw-v04-c03-p0032)</sub>
